news.title: STAT+: The 4 biggest ways the midterms could change health policy, according to policymakers, lobbyists, and experts
news.summary: No matter what happens on Election Day, the midterms will have sweeping implications for American health care. More than two dozen experts on what could come next.

news.title: Who’s responsible when clinical AI goes wrong? AMA weighs in
news.summary: The physician association, in a new framework, outlines its views on how different parties should bear responsibility for decisions, actions and failures involving clinical AI.

news.title: Fierce Healthcare Policy Brief: HHS launches breast cancer screening initiative; RHTP funds flow to 6 states
news.summary: The latest news from CMS and HHS this week: White House aims to improve breast cancer screening and early detection, PBM transparency rule finalized and six states receive RHTP funding.

news.title: Why Oscar Health is putting a focus on personalization for ACA exchange plans
news.summary: Another open enrollment period is set to begin on the Affordable Care Act's exchanges, and the team at Oscar Health is putting a focus on the unique ways it can innovate in this turbulent market.

news.title: Weekly Rundown: Doximity launches DoseCheck; AI recommends costlier care than doctors, study finds
news.summary: The latest news from Doximity, Hims & Hers, Google, NEJM AI, Eko Health, RevSpring, Symplr and Cleveland Clinic Cancer Institute.

news.title: Sutter Health calls off flagship hospital build in SF's East Bay, citing regulatory issues
news.summary: Sutter Health's planned $1 billion investment in Northern California's East Bay region will no longer include a new flagship medical center, at least for now. Outpatient investments in the community will still be going forward.

news.title: Alignment Healthcare lowers 2026 outlook as it navigates cost headwinds
news.summary: Alignment Healthcare is lowering its guidance for the year as it faces significant headwinds to finish out 2026.

news.title: Industry Voices—The other AI divide is already opening in healthcare
news.summary: Collaboration is necessary to head off the compounding divergence between hospitals that have the money, talent and infrastructure to put AI to work and those that don't, writes Abundant Venture Partners' Amanda DeMano.

news.title: Teladoc Health beats Q3 expectations as BetterHelp insurance growth accelerates
news.summary: Teladoc Health raised its 2026 outlook after better-than-expected third-quarter results, as BetterHelp’s insurance pivot gained traction and Integrated Care profitability improved.

news.title: Community Health Systems logs $86M net loss in Q3, hopes for return of 'pent-up' electives in 2027
news.summary: The for-profit hospital chain landed below internal and analyst expectations in the quarter due to now-familiar hurdles around elective surgeries and uninsured patients.

news.title: Tenet Healthcare sails past Q3 earnings estimates, boosts 2026 guidance
news.summary: Executives said the for-profit's outperformance stemmed from fundamentals like increased hospital volumes, checked expenses and increased ambulatory acuity.

news.title: BCBSMA, Medzown team up to match members with clinical trials
news.summary: Blue Cross Blue Shield of Massachusetts is teaming up with precision medicine company Medzown to make it easier for members with complex conditions participate in clinical trials.

news.title: Court rejects CMS' definition of 'medical frailty' under Medicaid work requirements
news.summary: A Massachusetts judge has sided with a coalition of states in an ongoing lawsuit over the rollout of Medicaid work requirements, and rejected the Trump administration's definition of "medical frailty" for critical exemptions.

news.title: Gilead reveals partial clinical hold on 2 CAR-T cell therapy trials
news.summary: Gilead Sciences announced on its third-quarter earnings call Oct. 29 that the company has placed a partial clinical hold on two studies for the CAR-T cell therapy KITE-753 in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL).

news.title: When drug development gets personal
news.summary: When Third Rock Ventures partner Jigar Raythatha was diagnosed with brain cancer, he found himself relying on a drug originally developed by Agios, a biotech his firm backed years before he joined. On "The Top Line," he shares how the experience changed his perspective on drug development.

news.title: Chutes & Ladders—Lilly unifies global markets as 36-year vet Patrik Jonsson retires
news.summary: Lilly will unite its U.S. and international commercial units as a long-time exec retires. Enanta's CEO will hang up his hat after 23 year at the helm. Estrella has tapped a new a CEO to lead it through a clinical trial.

news.title: Bracco invests $230M in first US diagnostic imaging manufacturing facility
news.summary: Bracco announced it will invest $230 million to establish its first U.S. manufacturing facility for injectable contrast media in Sanford, North Carolina.

news.title: Jazz's $820M Actio buyout gives rise to Setara, armed with $90M series A
news.summary: Setara Biosciences, a privately held spinout formed following Jazz Pharmaceuticals' acquisition of Actio Biosciences in September, has raised $90 million in series A financing to advance its clinical-stage neuroscience drug candidate and earlier-stage pipeline.

news.title: AstraZeneca cuts early-phase prostate cancer pipeline
news.summary: AstraZeneca has punted a pair of early-phase prostate cancer programs as part of its quarterly pipeline clear out.

news.title: Bambusa shoots past IPO targets as Aspen trims offering
news.summary: Bambusa Therapeutics has upsized its IPO, selling more shares at the midpoint of its target range to gross $168.9 million for bispecific R&D. But Aspen Neuroscience underperformed expectations, hitting the bottom end of its target range and selling slightly fewer shares than expected.

news.title: Roche launches differential diagnosis test for mesothelioma
news.summary: Roche announced the global launch of its VENTANA BAP1 (SP527) test, an automated, ready-to-use immunohistochemistry (IHC) assay.

news.title: Sanofi considering ‘moonshot’ treatments as M&A targets to survive Dupixent patent cliff
news.summary: Sanofi is considering “moonshot” treatments among the potential acquisition targets needed for the French pharma to urgently replenish its pipeline, Chief Financial Officer François-Xavier Roger told Fierce.

news.title: Molecular Partners to lay off up to 44% of workforce in radiotherapy pivot
news.summary: Molecular Partners plans to lay off up to 44% of its staff as it focuses its declining cash reserves on a radiotherapeutic pipeline led by an early-phase small cell lung cancer drug candidate.

news.title: Eli Lilly scraps phase 2 Alzheimer's program after drug falls short of expectations
news.summary: Eli Lilly has dropped its phase 2 Alzheimer's disease program for mevidalen, marking another setback for the experimental drug as the Big Pharma expands its neuroscience pipeline through multibillion-dollar acquisitions.

news.title: Merck outlines 2027 as ‘another year of investment’ despite recent clinical wins
news.summary: Even as a wave of clinical trial wins bolsters its momentum, Merck & Co. is prioritizing ongoing pipeline and commercial expansions over near-term margin growth, hoping to strengthen its long-term prospects past Keytruda's loss of exclusivity.

papers.title: HALO: Human-Grounded Granular Evaluation of Proactive Agents
papers.summary: Proactive agents must decide whether, when, and how far to assist without an explicit request. Existing evaluations often rely on automated scores or binary verdicts, offering limited human diagnosis of evidence use and intervention quality. To address these gaps, we introduce HALO, Human-Grounded GrAnular EvaLuation of PrOactive Agents. papers.title: RoboArchitect: Automating the Design of Robotic Agents with Persistent Memory
papers.summary: Recent work shows that a frozen robot policy performs far better inside an agent harness, where control code decides when to query the policy, consult vision tools, or command the arm directly. Yet today these harnesses are built by hand and redesigned for each new robot or benchmark. We show that harness design can be automated, offering a strong alternative to finetuning on a novel setup. papers.title: Your Benchmark Is an Empirical Measure Over Difficulty
papers.summary: A benchmark is not merely a collection of test questions; it naturally induces an empirical measure over difficulty. In this work, we develop this measure-based view of benchmark evaluation. This perspective allows us to identify and formalize two central failure modes: measure mismatch, where the benchmark difficulty distribution differs from the intended difficulty distribution, and coverage gaps, where uncovered regions along the difficulty axis prevent benchmarks from detecting meaningful localized training progress.
